reason: Source audit before any Protocol025 model result found that S5 registered periodic working-set release was implemented as a single finite cycle and its release_fraction=0.42 did not affect the curve; S4 floor_capacity_fraction=0.55 was not applied to the registered cache-miss CPU decay semantics. The revision makes implementation match already-registered physical meanings and strengthens the model-free audit. No model metric, D-C result, confirmation seed, or test seed was observed.

S4_semantic_fix.name: cache_warmup_decay
S4_semantic_fix.cpu_target_rule: age0 is unchanged familiar demand; warmup blends familiar CPU to 1.16*physical_cpu; decay then follows floor + (1.16-floor)*2^(-k/12) for 36 tail intervals, never reducing demand below familiar CPU
S4_semantic_fix.companion_rule: RAM and disk companions retain their pre-revision registered-source scaling but are explicitly audit metadata; floor_capacity_fraction is no longer misused as a substitute for the CPU decay floor
S4_semantic_fix.event_end_rule: after the registered 16+36 response window the task returns to familiar adapted demand

S5_semantic_fix.name: periodic_workingset_release
S5_semantic_fix.release_fraction_interpretation: fraction of peak-induced working-set excess released at the end of each cycle; 58% of the peak-induced excess remains before the next growth cycle
S5_semantic_fix.periodicity_rule: the 36-interval cycle repeats causally for the full available task trace rather than stopping after one period
S5_semantic_fix.age0_rule: age0 remains byte-identical to familiar adapted demand
S5_semantic_fix.ram_rule: within each cycle the excess grows to the registered 1.14*4GiB-Pi target, holds, then releases 42% of that induced excess over 6 intervals; demand is never reduced below familiar adapted RAM

S5 second-cycle check proves period 2 is nonzero and repeats period-1 geometry
S5 release_fraction check proves 0.42 changes the post-release excess
